Li Hongzhang as governor-general of Zhili
Acting Governor Shen Jinxiang of Hunan
Wang Qingmu, councillor of the Ministry of Commerce

claims.assessment: far-sighted founder of China Merchants Company

label.en: chief commissioner of sea transport for the Zhejiang bureau
Councillor of the Ministry of Commerce

translationRepairs: I have consulted the Zhejiang governor-general and governor, who have agreed to allocate two million shi of next year's tribute grain for transport to Tianjin by the new company's steamers, with freight charges, wastage allowances, and other terms to follow the established Sha-Ning regulations.

I have consulted the Zhejiang governor-general and governor, who have agreed to allocate two hundred thousand shi of next year's tribute grain for transport to Tianjin by the new company's steamers, with freight charges, wastage allowances, and other terms to follow the established Sha-Ning regulations.
s0026 漕米二十萬石 is 200,000 shi (二十萬 = 20 × 10,000); the prior idiomatic 'two million' invents an extra zero. The proposed two hundred thousand matches the Chinese.

Your servant has consulted with the Zhejiang governor-general and governor, who ordered allocation of two million shi of next year's tribute grain, to be transported to Tianjin by the merchants' recruitment steamers; freight, wastage grain, and other items shall all follow the fixed regulations for Sha-Ning boats.

Your servant has consulted with the Zhejiang governor-general and governor, who ordered allocation of two hundred thousand shi of next year's tribute grain, to be transported to Tianjin by the merchants' recruitment steamers; freight, wastage grain, and other items shall all follow the fixed regulations for Sha-Ning boats.
The same 二十萬石 means 200,000 shi; the prior literal's 'two million' is wrong, and the proposed two hundred thousand restores the numeral.

Zhu enlisted Circuit Intendant Hu Guangyong, Li Zhenyu, and others to solicit merchant investment, which met an enthusiastic response; Sheng brought in the Cantonese merchants Tang Jingsu and Xu Run to manage company affairs.

Zhu enlisted Circuit Intendant Hu Guangyong, Li Zhenyu, and others to solicit merchant investment, which met an enthusiastic response; Sheng brought in the Cantonese merchants Tang Tingshu and Xu Run to manage company affairs.
s0050 names 唐廷樞; 廷樞 romanizes as Tingshu, not Jingsu. The proposed Tang Tingshu corrects the mistransliteration while leaving the rest intact.

Qiang, through circuit intendant Hu Guangyong, Li Zhenyu, and others recruited merchant shares; those entering capital were extremely eager. Xuanhuai also brought in Cantonese Tang Jingsu and Xu Run to direct bureau affairs.

Qiang, through circuit intendant Hu Guangyong, Li Zhenyu, and others recruited merchant shares; those entering capital were extremely eager. Xuanhuai also brought in Cantonese Tang Tingshu and Xu Run to direct bureau affairs.
Literal likewise has Tang Jingsu for 唐廷樞; Tang Tingshu restores the correct reading of 廷樞.

Passenger and general cargo, together with all receipts and expenditures, were managed by Tang Jingsu and Xu Run, experienced merchants holding official rank; after each year's closing, detailed accounts were opened to all shareholders for inspection.

Passenger and general cargo, together with all receipts and expenditures, were managed by Tang Tingshu and Xu Run, experienced merchants holding official rank; after each year's closing, detailed accounts were opened to all shareholders for inspection.
s0082 again names 道員唐廷樞; Tang Tingshu is the correct romanization, and Tang Jingsu is the same mistransliteration.

Its taking passenger and general cargo, and income and expenditure accounts, are entrusted to circuit intendants Tang Jingsu and Xu Run, skilled in commerce, to preside over affairs; after each year's accounts settlement, detailed clear registers are opened and listed, all permitting subscribing merchants to read and audit.

Its taking passenger and general cargo, and income and expenditure accounts, are entrusted to circuit intendants Tang Tingshu and Xu Run, skilled in commerce, to preside over affairs; after each year's accounts settlement, detailed clear registers are opened and listed, all permitting subscribing merchants to read and audit.
The literal of s0082 likewise misreads 唐廷樞 as Tang Jingsu; Tang Tingshu corrects it.
The impeachment of Tang Jingsu and Zhu Qiang and the later exposure of Xu Run and Zhang Honglu offer clear proof.
The impeachment of Tang Tingshu and Zhu Qi'ang and the later exposure of Xu Run and Zhang Honglu offer clear proof.
s0144 has 唐廷樞、硃其昂: Tang Tingshu and Zhu Qi'ang. The prior idiomatic's Tang Jingsu and Zhu Qiang both misromanize the names; the proposed replacement restores both.
Such as Tang Jingsu and Zhu Qiang being impeached earlier, Xu Run and Zhang Honglu being exposed later—all are clear proof.
Such as Tang Tingshu and Zhu Qi'ang being impeached earlier, Xu Run and Zhang Honglu being exposed later—all are clear proof.
The proposal correctly changes Tang Jingsu to Tang Tingshu for 唐廷樞, but still leaves Zhu Qiang for 硃其昂. Revise to Zhu Qi'ang as well, matching the accepted idiomatic repair.

This past summer, while inspecting the receipt of the sea-transport tribute, I followed instructions from the Zongli Yamen and directed Prefect Zhu Qiang, the Zhejiang bureau's chief commissioner for sea transport, to draft regulations for steam navigation.

This past summer, while inspecting the receipt of the sea-transport tribute, I followed instructions from the Zongli Yamen and directed Prefect Zhu Qi'ang, the Zhejiang bureau's chief commissioner for sea transport, to draft regulations for steam navigation.
s0015 names 知府硃其昂; 其昂 is Qi'ang, so Zhu Qi'ang is required. Zhu Qiang drops the medial 其.
Zhu Qiang should be sent back to Shanghai to set up the bureau and recruit merchant investors.
Zhu Qi'ang should be sent back to Shanghai to set up the bureau and recruit merchant investors.
s0024 again has 硃其昂; Zhu Qi'ang restores the full given name, correcting Zhu Qiang.
That winter the company was formally established, with Prefect Zhu Qiang in charge and Circuit Intendant Sheng Xuanhuai as his deputy.
That winter the company was formally established, with Prefect Zhu Qi'ang in charge and Circuit Intendant Sheng Xuanhuai as his deputy.
s0049 has 知府硃其昂; the proposed Zhu Qi'ang correctly romanizes 其昂.
In 1875 Li Hongzhang memorialized for rewards to Zhu Qiang and his colleagues.
In 1875 Li Hongzhang memorialized for rewards to Zhu Qi'ang and his colleagues.
s0052's 其昂 is the same person 硃其昂; Zhu Qi'ang is the correct full romanization against prior Zhu Qiang.
Moreover Yunnan's copper, Sichuan's lampwood, Jiangsu and Zhejiang's government-procured goods, Zhili and Shan's relief grain—all were managed by bureau ships.
Moreover Yunnan's copper, Sichuan's lampwood, Jiangsu and Zhejiang's government-procured goods, Zhili and Shanxi's relief grain—all were managed by bureau ships.
s0121 直、晉之賑糧 pairs Zhili with 晉 (Shanxi). The literal's 'Shan' truncates the province name; Shanxi matches the idiomatic and the Chinese.
